methodological_rigor.justification: The HOVON-902 prospective multicenter national cohort is well-designed with pre-specified statistical analysis plan, uniform first-line treatment (96% R-CHOP), and 46-center real-world enrollment. PhasED-Seq PV identification succeeded in 99% of patients. The exclusion criteria are clearly defined and a CONSORT diagram is provided. Multivariate Cox models controlling for IPI and EOT PET-CT confirm MRD independence. Minor limitations include non-central PET-CT review and variable EOT plasma collection timing. Sample size (n=134) is modest but adequate for the hazard ratios observed.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a prospective validation cohort study (Oxford LoE 2b) with direct clinical relevance to LBCL management. The findings demonstrate that ctDNA-MRD with PhasED-Seq provides superior PPV compared to PET-CT (68% vs 56%) and could guide clinical decision-making in EOT assessment. The data support NCCN guidelines (category 2B) and align with ongoing MRD-directed clinical trials (ALPHA3, GO43075). The result that all non-CMR/MRD-positive patients relapsed within 3 years has immediate implications for clinical trial design and patient selection.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript adheres well to STROBE guidelines for cohort studies: eligibility criteria, enrollment diagram, baseline characteristics, follow-up duration, and loss-to-follow-up are all reported. Statistical methods are detailed and pre-specified (SAP referenced). Limitations section is comprehensive. Data Supplement is referenced repeatedly for additional analyses. However, primary data are not publicly deposited in a recognized repository, and code availability is not stated, limiting full reproducibility.

novelty_literature.justification: This study validates PhasED-Seq-based ctDNA-MRD in a prospective real-world cohort, building directly on earlier work by Kurtz et al. (2021) and Roschewski et al. (2025). The novelty lies in the uniformly treated, multicenter, real-world design which addresses the limitation of prior single-center or clinical trial populations. The finding that MRD positivity within CMR patients identifies a high-risk subgroup is a meaningful extension. However, the overall conclusion—that ultrasensitive ctDNA-MRD is prognostic in LBCL—was already established; this study primarily strengthens existing evidence in a more generalizable setting.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly organized with logical progression from introduction through methods, results, and discussion. Statistical results are reported with appropriate precision (HRs, 95% CIs, p-values). Figure descriptions are informative. The discussion appropriately contextualizes findings within current literature and guidelines, and the limitations section is unusually thorough. Minor tightening possible in the discussion section.

key_strengths: Prospective, multicenter, national real-world cohort (46 centers) with uniform first-line treatment, directly addressing the generalizability gap of prior trial-population studies
Pre-specified statistical analysis plan with comprehensive multivariate models confirming independent prognostic value of MRD over IPI and PET-CT
99% PV identification success rate demonstrates practical clinical applicability of PhasED-Seq
Strong hazard ratios (PFS HR 9.8, OS HR 7.7) with highly significant p-values supporting robust prognostic discrimination
Thorough limitations section and contextual alignment with NCCN guidelines and ongoing clinical trials
key_concerns: Modest sample size (n=134) limits statistical power for subgroup analyses, particularly in the CMR/MRD-positive subset (n=9)
Non-central PET-CT review introduces interobserver variability that may affect PET-CT performance estimates
Primary data not deposited in a public repository; code availability not stated
Variable EOT plasma collection timing and COVID-19-related protocol deviations may introduce confounding
Mechanism explaining persistent MRD positivity without relapse in 8 patients is not fully explored
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a solid prospective validation study of ctDNA-MRD in a real-world LBCL cohort with strong statistical evidence and direct clinical relevance; it merits Tier 2 consideration with minor revisions to address data availability and subgroup analysis limitations.
